title: Influence of DEM Resolution on the Hydrological Responses of a Terraced Catchment: An Exploratory Modelling Approach
publication_date_basis: Published online 2022-12-28; the journal volume is Remote Sensing 2023, 15, 169. The benchmark freezes the first public publication year for the hard time window.
datasets: UAV airborne-lidar point cloud and 0.1 m, 0.25 m, 0.5 m and 1 m bare-earth DEMs

study_area_verified.name: Braçal experimental catchment, Silva Escura, Sever do Vouga municipality, central Portugal
study_area_verified.land_cover: eucalyptus-dominated forest catchment with bench terraces
study_area_verified.lidar_acquisition: UAV lidar collected in November 2021 using a DJI Matrice 300 and YellowScan Mapper
study_area_verified.source: replacement seed full text, Materials and Methods sections 2.1-2.4

anchor_use_verified.role: airborne-lidar ground returns are filtered into bare-earth DEMs at 0.1 m, 0.25 m, 0.5 m and 1 m and then used for drainage extraction, terrain representation and SWAT hydrological modelling
anchor_use_verified.evidence: The Methods state that the iterative ground filtering produced 0.1 m, 0.25 m, 0.5 m and 1 m bare earth DEMs and that the four very-high-resolution DEMs were based on a LiDAR survey.
anchor_use_verified.catalog_relation: USGS/3DEP/1m is a catalog analogue for the same one-metre airborne-lidar bare-earth elevation observation. It is not the Portuguese project dataset and does not cover the seed study area.

runtime_region_transfer.runtime_region: Huron Creek watershed, Michigan, United States
runtime_region_transfer.reason: The ready catalog Anchor is US-only. The prior Huron Creek region is retained to keep the benchmark input executable; no claim is made that USGS 3DEP covers the Portuguese seed site.

idea.research_question: How does the spatial resolution and acquisition lineage of fine bare-earth elevation alter drainage representation and hydrological response in a terraced catchment?
idea.hypothesis: One-metre-or-finer airborne-lidar bare-earth DEMs preserve terrace geometry and drainage connectivity better than coarser or photogrammetric surfaces, producing measurably different watershed boundaries, stream networks and simulated streamflow responses.
idea.mechanism: Airborne-lidar ground filtering resolves terrace risers, channels and local flow barriers. Aggregation progressively removes these features, changing slope, flow direction, contributing area and stream topology; those terrain changes propagate into SWAT hydrologic response units and simulated runoff timing and magnitude.

key_variables.target: terrain-representation accuracy, drainage-network agreement and hydrological-model performance across DEM resolutions
predictors: bare-earth DEM resolution and acquisition lineage
drainage density, sinuosity and bifurcation ratio

data_sources: UAV airborne-lidar point clouds and derived bare-earth DEMs
idea.analytical_approach: Construct or aggregate terrain grids from a qualifying one-metre airborne-lidar source, derive terrain and drainage metrics consistently at each resolution, run matched hydrological-model configurations, and attribute changes in simulated response to resolution-driven changes in terrain representation while holding non-terrain inputs fixed.
idea.expected_contribution: A reproducible assessment of when metre-scale airborne-lidar terrain materially changes hydrological inference and which terrain structures are lost under aggregation.
idea.falsification_condition: The hypothesis is rejected if lidar resolution produces no reproducible improvement in terrain or drainage representation and no material, independently validated change in hydrological performance after non-terrain inputs and calibration are held constant.
